match.reason: No bank point covers the new point's content: e-fiscal only defines direct and indirect taxes in passing within fiscal policy, and nothing in the bank covers progressive, regressive or proportional taxes or income from government businesses and asset sales.

draft.title: Government revenue
card: a tax on income or wealth, paid straight to the government by the person or firm it is aimed at. Personal income tax and company tax are examples.
a tax on spending, collected by sellers and passed on to the government. The goods and services tax (GST) is an example.
A tax is progressive if the share of income paid in tax rises as income rises. It is proportional if the share stays the same. It is regressive if the share falls as income rises.
Governments also earn revenue from government businesses and from selling assets. Selling an asset brings in money once, so it is not a steady source.
draft.remember: Taxes on income are direct and taxes on spending are indirect. The tax rate pattern decides if it is progressive, proportional or regressive.

a.q: Which of these is an indirect tax?
opts: A tax added to the price of goods bought in shops
A tax taken from the wages a worker earns
A tax paid by a company on its yearly profit
A tax raised on the income a person gets from savings
a.why: An indirect tax is placed on spending and collected by the seller, as the GST is. The other three are taxes on income or profit, so they are direct taxes.
a.clue: Think about which tax is collected when you buy something.

b.q: Every worker in Ballarat pays a flat 10% of their income in a levy. Rima earns $40,000 and Tom earns $120,000. What type of tax is this?
opts: Proportional, as both pay the same share of income
Progressive, as Tom pays more dollars than Rima
Regressive, as Rima has less income left over after tax
Indirect, as the levy is paid by many different workers
b.why: Both workers pay 10% of their income, so the share stays the same as income rises. That makes it proportional. Tom pays more dollars, but a tax is progressive only if the share rises with income.
b.clue: Compare the share of income paid, not the dollars paid.

a.best: A tax added to the price of goods bought in shops

b.best: Proportional, as both pay the same share of income
